claims.text: AlCoCrFeNi is a high-entropy alloy containing multiple principal elements.
AlCoCrFeNi will exhibit superior elevated-temperature tribo-corrosion resistance compared with conventional structural alloys.
The multiple principal elements in AlCoCrFeNi enable stable protective oxide layers to form during simultaneous mechanical wear and corrosion.
The proposed starting material is a homogenized bulk AlCoCrFeNi sample.
The proposed starting material has a defect-minimized microstructure.
Protective oxide scales will form rapidly at wear interfaces under the proposed conditions.
The oxide scales formed at wear interfaces will be adherent.
Elemental segregation may reinforce the integrity of the oxide scale.
Multiple principal elements promote adaptive oxidation in AlCoCrFeNi.
Adaptive oxidation produces a stable oxide scale.
The stable oxide scale reduces active sites for corrosion.
The stable oxide scale mitigates wear-induced microstructural damage.
AlCoCrFeNi will have a lower mass-loss rate than conventional alloys under identical high-temperature tribo-corrosion conditions.
AlCoCrFeNi will develop shallower wear tracks than conventional alloys under identical high-temperature tribo-corrosion conditions.
AlCoCrFeNi will sustain less corrosion damage than conventional alloys under identical high-temperature tribo-corrosion conditions.
The predicted benefits are limited to the specified temperature and tribo-corrosion regime.
The performance of AlCoCrFeNi may vary outside the specified parameters or in different environmental chemistries.
